cells.tense: You are setting something down because it is finished, and you have the pen.
cells.act: give it what it needs today, not what it is scheduled for
cells.ask: Choose something you're tending. Give it what it actually needs today, not what you had planned for it — and if that's nothing, give it nothing.
cells.core:
Something is done, and your hand is already off it. What's left is caring for what's still growing here — the part that comes after, when the cleared space gets filled with something tended rather than something gripped. That's the part people skip. You're not skipping it.

Tending, done right, doesn't exhaust you. It asks what the thing needs now, then it stops asking. So give one thing what it actually needs today, not what you scheduled. Maybe that's less than the plan. Maybe it's nothing. Care that doesn't clutch looks like that, and you can tell by how you feel at the end — emptied out, or still full.
cells.sheetLine: What's finished is finished. Tend what's left.
cells.verb: Setting down what's finished, on purpose
cells.place: The table where things get weighed and brought back level

cells.tense: You will hand it over early to prove you are not clinging, and nobody asked.
cells.act: do the small practice again, alone, today
cells.ask: Repeat the one plain practice, by yourself, even if it feels pointless. One run of it, no plan on top, no refining.
cells.core:
Here the release runs out past the thing. You're handing over what isn't finished, and from where others stand it can look like discipline — refusing first so it can't be refused to you, giving up before anyone can ask. That's not release. It's bracing, and it hollows out the same table it was meant to keep level.

What steadies it is smaller than what you've been doing. Repeat the plain practice, by yourself, and make the repetition the whole point. No refinement to show, no plan built on top, just the session done the same way it was done yesterday. Solitude like that connects. It doesn't isolate, and it doesn't need anyone watching to count.
cells.sheetLine: You're giving things up before they're done.
cells.verb: Setting down what's finished, on purpose
cells.place: The table where things get weighed and brought back level

cells.tense: You were still holding it long after it had already ended, and you knew.
cells.act: carry it without tightening around it
cells.ask: Hold it the way you'd hold something you didn't have to grip — same weight, looser hand — and see how much lighter it sits.
cells.core:
You've held this a long time, and holding it has become the thing itself. The grip is tight enough that you can't tell any more which parts are the load and which are your hands. It's exhausting in a way that doesn't show, and the balance here has been off for a while.

You don't have to put it down today to get somewhere. Keep bearing the weight, but stop squeezing it. Same weight, looser hand — that's the whole act, and it's enough for one day. Strength that's healthy contains what it holds. It doesn't crush the thing, and it doesn't crush you.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding it so tight you can't feel your hands.
cells.verb: Setting down what's finished, on purpose
cells.place: The table where things get weighed and brought back level

cells.tense: The surrender has already happened and you are still writing it as something you might do.
cells.act: make room for it without steering it
cells.ask: Make room for something that's growing without steering it. Give it the space, then leave it alone and don't check on it.
cells.core:
Some release already happened here, quietly, without a decision you can point to. You'd probably describe it as still pending. The hand that set it down was yours, and the account in your head doesn't list it, so the credit for the clearing has gone unclaimed. When it goes well, you notice room where there used to be strain — a thing that gets to grow because nobody is hovering over it.

Caring for what's growing works better than managing it. Make room for one thing, then leave it be — no steering, no checking on it before the day is out. That's tending without clutching, and it's the shape of what you already did. You just haven't put your name on it yet.
cells.sheetLine: You already let it go. You're still calling it pending.
cells.verb: Setting down what's finished, on purpose
cells.place: The table where things get weighed and brought back level

attempts.check: The claim the record doesn't support is any account of what was let go of or held onto and for how long, so all four cores stay in the present of the grip and say nothing about history, people, or what it cost. A reader could reasonably say the release was long ago and already grieving, or that the holding is somebody else's weight; the asks survive both because each is one small act done today and teaches something about the person's own hand on it even if the read is wrong. The line that serves me more than them is 'surrender as fulfillment, not defeat' — it flatters the card's own language, so it stays out of the glass.
